key_insight: An uncertainty-aware framework translates predicted patient deterioration risk into ICU staffing plans while accounting for hiring delays and extreme shortage risk.
clinical_relevance: The approach could support ICU workforce planning by balancing staffing costs against shortage exposure, but patient-care benefits remain unproven.
method: Model dynamic uncertainty in patient risk estimates without changing the predictive model.
Use Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) to assess extreme shortage exposure.
Feed risk-calibrated demand into hourly rolling-horizon scheduling with operational constraints.
evidence_signal: Evaluation on realistic MIMIC-IV trajectories showed a favorable cost–shortage trade-off versus deterministic and reactive baselines, with stress tests assessing robustness to calibration drift.
watch_item: Real-world deployment needs prospective validation; the abstract reports no patient outcomes or numerical effect sizes.
paper_title: From Clinical Risk Prediction to Operational Decisions: An Uncertainty-Aware Framework for ICU Staffing
